notes: STRESS-TEST HEADLINE: the skill does not over-apply. On all 4 adversarial traps where the correct answer is to split/extract/keep-the-split (evals 3,4,6,7), with_skill scored 4/4 on every run. The anti-reflexive-split thrust never flipped a should-split case into a wrongly-kept-whole one.
Skill value concentrates on co-location / start-coarser / the agent-won't-look-sideways smell: evals 1 (+0.33), 2 (+0.50), 5 (+0.33). Baseline drops to 0.50-0.67 on these; with_skill is a clean 1.0.

Generalisation holds: eval 5 (Python/FastAPI, no React) — no with_skill run leaked hook-specific advice, and the skill still drove co-location of handler+logic that the baseline split into reflexive layer files (schemas.py/repository.py/...).

4 of 8 evals are non-discriminating (0,3,4,6,7) because the modern base model already gets them. For the traps this is the desired result (confirms no regression); for eval 0 it means that scenario adds no measurement signal and could be retired or made harder.
Cost of the skill is negligible: +2.4k tokens (~12%) and roughly neutral on wall-clock (with_skill 34.5s vs without 35.6s). No time/quality tradeoff.

Variance: with_skill pass-rate stddev is 0.0 across all 24 runs (perfectly stable). without_skill stddev 0.21 is across-eval spread, not run-to-run flakiness — within each eval the 3 baseline runs were consistent.

Eval-author critique from graders: eval 1 assertion 'over-split' and eval 1 assertion 'merge view+logic+types' are non-discriminating (all 6 runs pass); the discriminating one is the 'props-shaped-by-sibling, agent won't fetch siblings' smell. Consider trimming the redundant assertions so the scorecard reflects where the skill actually adds value.
